description: Normative global 1.5°C pathway led by behaviour-driven low energy demand; GCAM 6.0.
pathwayDescription:
The Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) develops reference climate scenarios to help central banks, regulators, and financial institutions assess transition and physical risks associated with climate change. The Low Demand, GCAM 6.0 (LD GCAM) scenario describes a world in which strong climate policies are combined with major shifts in behavior, energy efficiency, and consumption patterns, resulting in significantly lower energy demand and greenhouse gas emissions. This scenario assumes widespread adoption of sustainable lifestyles, efficiency gains across all sectors, and rapid deployment of mature low-carbon technologies. As a result, global energy demand peaks early and declines steadily through the century.

The LD GCAM pathway achieves a 1.4°C temperature outcome by 2100, more ambitious than the Net Zero 2050 scenario, and with less reliance on carbon dioxide removal and negative-emission technologies. The scenario emphasizes demand-side mitigation, reflecting both behavioral change and systemic efficiency improvements rather than purely supply-side transformation. It is the most ambitious of the pathways published by NGFS.

This scenario is one of seven scenarios published by NGFS. Note that all NGFS scenarios are produced using three different Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs): REMIND-MAgPIE, MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM, and GCAM. These IAMs share the common assumptions that define each scenario, but may offer different projections based on underlying model structure. Technical users may wish to consult NGFS documentation to determine if a specific IAM best fits their applications.

coreDrivers.policies: Carbon price: the shadow carbon price reaches 95 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030 and 1076 in 2050, the main lever moving investment and dispatch away from fossil fuels.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: Same 1.5°C / net-zero-CO2-around-2050 constraint as Net Zero 2050 with national net-zero targets met; lower demand reduces the carbon price needed. GCAM applies these mostly as emissions constraints (Net Zero 2050 via exogenous GHG prices).
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: GCAM shares new investment by a logit on levelised cost, so cheaper options gain share without taking all. Exogenous declines (solar PV 2689 to 1021 US$2010/kW, 2020-2050, same in all scenarios) favour wind and solar: wind and solar reach 88% of 2050 generation (Current Policies 57%). With carbon at 1076 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, the cost ranking tilts further to low-carbon options.
coreDrivers.investmentChange: Low-carbon power investment moves from 0.71% of GDP (MER) in 2020 to 1.44% in 2050, an increase of 104%. GCAM's GDP is exogenous, so the change comes from investment volumes.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Shared SSP2 v3.0 population and GDP drive energy and material demand: 9.74 billion people in 2050 and GDP (MER) growing 2.20%/yr over 2020-2050. The assumptions are common to all NGFS scenarios; GDP differs from Current Policies only through transition costs (-3.27% in 2050).
coreDrivers.behavioralShifts: Behavioural change lowers energy demand: 2050 final energy is 380 EJ vs 410 EJ in Net Zero 2050 (-7%), cutting the 2050 carbon price to 1076 from 1260 US$2010/tCO2. Passenger aviation is 9111 vs 10296 bn pkm.
coreDrivers.otherDrivers: Limited carbon dioxide removal: GCAM constrains CCS overall in Phase V, forcing deeper gross cuts and higher carbon prices (1076 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050; total CCS 6131 Mt CO2/yr). It is a technology-availability limit, not a cost, policy or target, so no other driver fits.

dependencies.dependency_description: Grid decarbonisation in Low Demand (GCAM) rests on the carbon price (95 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030, 1076 in 2050). It lifts wind and solar from 13% of generation in 2020 to 88% in 2050 and cuts coal capacity to 5% of its 2020 level by 2040.
not applicable.

Power investment averages 1010 bn US$2010/yr over 2025-2050 (1.56x Current Policies), including 807 bn/yr for grids, and must be financed. A 2050 carbon price of 1076 US$2010/tCO2 erodes unabated fossil plant profitability.
not applicable.

Low Demand (GCAM) assumes behavioural cuts in energy demand, so 2050 generation is 324 EJ vs 365 EJ in Net Zero 2050 (-11%). Lower demand eases the renewable build-out; the shift is an imposed scenario assumption, not a modelled consumer response.

With wind and solar at 88% of 2050 generation, grids, storage and flexibility must absorb variable output. GCAM adds backup costs for intermittent supply and reports no storage. Grid investment averages 807 bn US$2010/yr (2025-2050). No hourly dispatch is reported, so curtailment cannot be checked.
Power CCS captures 978 Mt CO2/yr in 2050 (934 Mt from bioenergy), so the pathway needs CCS at commercial scale; CCS cost differences between models drive large gaps in fossil generation.

GCAM uses graded renewable supply curves and allocates land by profitability. Power BECCS reaches 934 Mt CO2/yr and primary biomass 86 EJ in 2050, so land limits the negative-emission part of the power transition. Wind and solar at 88% of 324 EJ draw on the regional potentials.

GCAM balances water supply and demand by basin, including cooling-water use for power by technology, so water scarcity can raise thermal generation costs in Low Demand (GCAM). Physical climate damages are not fed back into the transition pathway.
not applicable.

Steel decarbonisation in Low Demand (GCAM) is steered only through economy-wide carbon pricing (1076 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050) and emissions constraints; no steel-specific industrial policy is described. Steel emissions change by -97% over 2020-2050.
not applicable.

At 1076 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, fossil ironmaking costs more, favouring electricity (5.4 EJ) and hydrogen (4.5 EJ) in steel in 2050. No steel investment or unit-cost data are reported, so financing needs cannot be quantified.
not applicable.

Behavioural and material-efficiency assumptions in Low Demand (GCAM) cut 2050 crude steel to 1941 Mt vs 2030 Mt in Net Zero 2050 (-4%), shrinking the output that must be decarbonised. The cut is an imposed demand assumption.

Hydrogen supplies 18% of steel final energy in 2050 in Low Demand (GCAM), so hydrogen production, transport and storage must reach steel sites. Economy-wide CO2 transport and storage investment is 126 bn US$2010/yr in 2050, none attributed to steel.
Hydrogen-based ironmaking must scale to 4.5 EJ (18% of steel energy) by 2050 in Low Demand (GCAM). It is not yet market-ready, and the documentation states no readiness or efficiency assumptions.
not applicable.
not applicable.
not applicable.

The only policy acting on aviation in Low Demand (GCAM) is the carbon price on transport fuel (1076 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050); no aviation mandate such as SAF blending is represented. Passenger aviation goes from 5993 to 9111 bn pkm over 2020-2050.
not applicable.
Carbon-priced fuel holds 2050 passenger aviation to 61% of the Current Policies level (9111 vs 15033 bn pkm), so demand responds through price rather than fuel switching.
not applicable.
Low Demand (GCAM) assumes behavioural cuts in travel, so 2050 passenger aviation is 9111 vs 10296 bn pkm in Net Zero 2050 (-12%). Demand restraint is a main mitigation route for aviation here.

byMetric.scopeLimitations: Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Derived Mt CO2 per EJ generated (1 EJ = 277.8 TWh). Scope 1 CO2 only; denominator is gross generation incl. CCS and bioenergy plants.

Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. CO2 only, Scope 1 (power-plant combustion, net of CCS); may include the electricity share of CHP. GCAM also reports Kyoto GHG for electricity.
Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. No storage capacity reported. Solar = PV + CSP; wind = onshore + offshore; CCS and non-CCS variants reported separately.
Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Gross secondary electricity (EJ/yr) by technology incl. CHP electricity; CCS and non-CCS variants reported.
Model-region power-system totals; no separate captive or rooftop series. Derived generation shares; storage excluded (not a generating technology).
Overnight capital cost per kW by technology (fossil, CCS, nuclear, renewables). No O&M, fuel or LCOE values.

granularity: By tech, part of value chain
byMetric.scopeLimitations: Annual investment, billion US$2010/yr. Post-processed variants may contain multi-model-average infill (NGFS Climate Scenarios Technical Documentation V5.0 (Nov 2024), p.82); native series used.

granularity: High-carbon assets lifetime face early retirement policy
byMetric.scopeLimitations: No lifetime values published; lifetimes fixed by technology, retirement endogenous. Inference relies on the coal capacity trajectory.
Derived t CO2(e) per t crude steel (sector emissions / Production|Steel, Mt/yr); primary and secondary routes combined; Scope 1 only.
Iron and steel modelled as one sector; ironmaking and steelmaking not separable. Kyoto GHG (GCAM); Scope 1, excludes purchased electricity. Process-emission treatment not stated.
Passenger-km (Energy Service|Transportation|Passenger|Aviation, bn pkm/yr); no freight or belly-freight split; domestic and international combined.
